The collector is now physically specified, and its main obstruction is chemical selectivity

I chose relocation of an existing divacancy into a buried layer, followed by cooling to retain its position as the post-assembly operation. The destination is a negatively charged acceptor layer in 3C-SiC. Its electric field, carrier populations, defect charge states, mobility and equilibrium attraction are calculated together.

The important result is that strengthening this collector also favours competing chemistry. The well attracts the desired positively charged divacancy, but it stabilizes a doubly charged antisite intermediate more strongly. At sufficiently low local Fermi level, the published formation energies also favour separated, more highly charged fragmentation products.

That is a substantive obstruction to selective capture. It does not establish rapid destruction: the charged escape pathway still decides the rate. I have therefore retained the connected mobility calculation and the failed selective-purification application, while replacing an assumed intact-defect trajectory with a quantitative test of chemical survival.

All performance comparisons below use charge-equilibrated transport. The earlier 44-fold frozen-charge comparison supplies no treatment advantage.

1. A destination that pays for its field and its retention

The proposed operation has four parts:

A buried Al-doped layer supplies negative fixed charge.
Annealing permits existing divacancies to move through the two complementary pivot routes.
The resulting band bending biases their spatial distribution toward the layer.
Cooling arrests whichever defects actually occupy the target region at the stopping time.

The target remains reversible while hot. I did not turn arrival into an absorbing event or assume feedback that stops each defect separately.

There is a particularly relevant realised precedent: electric-field-assisted accumulation of hydrogen in buried Al-doped regions of 4H-SiC. Janson and colleagues observed deuterium accumulation after implantation and annealing and explained it through positively charged hydrogen entering the doped layer. Thus, buried electrostatic collection itself is established; the prospective distinction here is relocation of an existing, useful defect complex while retaining its chemistry.

Three qualifications prevent this from becoming an unjustified destruction claim:

These are zero-temperature electronic formation energies. Vibrational free energies can move the crossing.
Separated-defect energies do not supply the short-range escape pathway.
The charged fragments repel one another. Two 
+

+2 fragments have a continuum Coulomb interaction of approximately 0.59 eV at 1 nm separation using the same dielectric constant. That contribution cannot be discarded when joining the bound intermediate to the separated endpoint.

Mixing entropy must also enter a full dissociation equilibrium. A positive standard formation-energy difference alone does not establish stability at a particular dilute defect concentration.

The conclusion is therefore specific: the collector needs kinetic protection against a chemically plausible, increasingly favourable fragmentation branch. Constraining a simulation to intact divacancies would remove precisely the process that can reverse the result.

The times are uncertain; the weak collection result is not merely a slow-clock artefact

The published neutral silicon-vacancy pivot has a calculated activation-free-energy reduction of 0.37 eV at 1,500 K. Charged-path entropy corrections were not acquired in that study. 
link.aps.org

As a source-based sensitivity test, I extrapolated that one correction linearly to 1,200 K, giving 0.296 eV, and left the other corrections unchanged. This is deliberately a partial correction:

the best stopping time fell from about 470 to 61 hours;
the peak target occupation changed from 20.1% to 21.1%.

Giving both fast pivot legs the same correction shortened the time further but left the peak near 20%. Thus, accelerating the clock is not sufficient to turn this collector into reliable placement.

Nor is 20% a global ceiling. Stronger layers collected more. An especially narrow, assumed 5 nm layer with ten times the Al inventory reached about 51% at 3,000 hours and was still improving. That case requires a sharper construction, has a larger population of the antisite intermediate, and places the centre in the fragmentation-favoured energetic regime. It cannot be granted those resources without their chemical consequences.

Cooling can retain a successful position without an irreversible chemical trap. Under the baseline two-charge rates, even maintaining the maximum 1,200 K diffusivity for an additional minute would add only about 0.73 nm of three-dimensional RMS displacement. This supplies a conditional cooling requirement; it does not establish an experimental cooling cycle or increase the fraction that arrived.

The annealing, charge-assisted formation and feedback-placement results are experimentally realised benchmarks. Their numerical performance cannot simply be transferred between materials or equated with relocation of an existing complex. 
researchgate.net
+2

The prospective distinction remains worthwhile: moving existing complexes without a new vacancy-generation step. But this construction currently supplies a conditional layer-collection operation. It does not yet supply reliable individual placement, preservation of useful silicon-vacancy spectators, or restoration of a neutral spin-active readout state inside the Al-rich destination.

I am retaining the collector calculation and its failures, while moving the scientific emphasis from the mobility optimum to selectivity of the complete translation-and-escape network. The requirements are now concrete:

the attractive destination must remain compatible with the transition states that carry translation;
the same destination must not make a competing chemical family overwhelmingly easier to reach;
escape must be suppressed over the accumulated residence in every reactive waypoint;
the atoms producing the destination must have compatible local chemistry.

The present evidence establishes those coupled constraints and gives quantitative escape-barrier targets. It does not yet establish a superior atomic-placement treatment. Further work earns its value by changing or acquiring that chemical interface; another adjustment of the Fermi-level setting cannot substitute for it.

html:
The collector is now physically specified, and its main obstruction is chemical selectivity

I chose relocation of an existing divacancy into a buried layer, followed by cooling to retain its position as the post-assembly operation. The destination is a negatively charged acceptor layer in 3C-SiC. Its electric field, carrier populations, defect charge states, mobility and equilibrium attraction are calculated together.

The important result is that strengthening this collector also favours competing chemistry. The well attracts the desired positively charged divacancy, but it stabilizes a doubly charged antisite intermediate more strongly. At sufficiently low local Fermi level, the published formation energies also favour separated, more highly charged fragmentation products.

That is a substantive obstruction to selective capture. It does not establish rapid destruction: the charged escape pathway still decides the rate. I have therefore retained the connected mobility calculation and the failed selective-purification application, while replacing an assumed intact-defect trajectory with a quantitative test of chemical survival.

All performance comparisons below use charge-equilibrated transport. The earlier 44-fold frozen-charge comparison supplies no treatment advantage.

1. A destination that pays for its field and its retention

The proposed operation has four parts:

  1. A buried Al-doped layer supplies negative fixed charge.
  2. Annealing permits existing divacancies to move through the two complementary pivot routes.
  3. The resulting band bending biases their spatial distribution toward the layer.
  4. Cooling arrests whichever defects actually occupy the target region at the stopping time.

The target remains reversible while hot. I did not turn arrival into an absorbing event or assume feedback that stops each defect separately.

There is a particularly relevant realised precedent: electric-field-assisted accumulation of hydrogen in buried Al-doped regions of 4H-SiC. Janson and colleagues observed deuterium accumulation after implantation and annealing and explained it through positively charged hydrogen entering the doped layer. Thus, buried electrostatic collection itself is established; the prospective distinction here is relocation of an existing, useful defect complex while retaining its chemistry. Phys. Rev. B

One semiconductor potential determines both attraction and transport

The electron electrochemical potential μe\mu_eμe​ is uniform at equilibrium; the spatial variation comes from band bending. With u=eϕ/kBTu=e\phi/k_BTu=eϕ/kB​T,

n(x)=n∞eu(x),p(x)=p∞e−u(x).n(x)=n_\infty e^{u(x)},\qquad p(x)=p_\infty e^{-u(x)}.n(x)=n∞​eu(x),p(x)=p∞​e−u(x).

I solved Poisson’s equation with those carriers, the donor background and the ionization of the acceptors. The Al charge was not held fixed when its occupation should change.

The principal finite-layer calculation used:

The dielectric constant, density-of-states parameters and acceptor energy come from the semiconductor parameter literature. The layer dimensions and initial distribution are construction assumptions. pure.coventry.ac.uk

This calculation gives:

  • a potential depression of approximately 0.424 V;
  • a central local Fermi coordinate of 0.734 eV;
  • a maximum field of approximately 5.85 MV/m;
  • an ionized acceptor inventory of approximately 9.67×1011 cm−29.67\times10^{11}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}9.67×1011 cm−2.

The finite profile matters. Published Al-doped 3C-SiC multilayers demonstrate controllable doping and reduced incorporation tails, but they do not establish an arbitrary delta layer. In the best profile shown by Colston and colleagues, the plotted decay length is roughly 13 nm per decade. I used that evidence to reject a zero-width sheet as an acquired construction; a 20 nm Gaussian remains a specified approximation, not a demonstrated assembly. wrap.warwick.ac.uk

There is also a parameter correction worth retaining. The 2017 parameter paper prints a band-gap coefficient of 6×10−36\times10^{-3}6×10−3 alongside an equation that would then give a negative gap at 1,200 K. I did not import that combination. I used 2.03 eV as an explicit high-temperature gap assumption, then repeated the calculation over 2.00–2.20 eV while holding the dopant background fixed. This is a sensitivity interval, not a claimed experimental uncertainty range.

2. The stronger well starts selecting the wrong chemical family

The relevant intended intermediate is

U=CSi(VC)2,U=\mathrm{C_{Si}(V_C)_2},U=CSi​(VC​)2​,

the carbon antisite with two carbon vacancies, called VCV in the source papers. It permits one of the divacancy’s pivot motions.

A chemically balanced competing endpoint is

VV⟶CAV+VC,\mathrm{VV} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CAV}+V_C,VV⟶CAV+VC​,

where CAV=CSiVC\mathrm{CAV}=\mathrm{C_{Si}V_C}CAV=CSi​VC​. This conserves the missing Si and C inventory but destroys the divacancy as a useful defect species.

For this comparison, it is essential to restore the absolute formation-energy reference. Adding two energies that were each shifted to make neutral VV zero would give an incorrect reaction energy. I recalibrated the published supplementary figure against its energy axis before adding the separated-product energies. The resulting approximate zero-temperature formation energies are

Ef(VV+)≃6.63+E,Ef(CAV2+)≃3.40+2E,Ef(VC2+)≃1.18+2E,\begin{aligned} E_f(\mathrm{VV}^{+})&\simeq6.63+E,\\ E_f(\mathrm{CAV}^{2+})&\simeq3.40+2E,\\ E_f(V_C^{2+})&\simeq1.18+2E, \end{aligned}Ef​(VV+)Ef​(CAV2+)Ef​(VC2+​)​≃6.63+E,≃3.40+2E,≃1.18+2E,​

Consequently, for widely separated products,

ΔEf∘[VV+→CAV2++VC2+]≃−2.05+3E\boxed{ \Delta E_f^\circ \bigl[ \mathrm{VV}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{CAV}^{2+}+V_C^{2+} \bigr] \simeq -2.05+3E }ΔEf∘​[VV+→CAV2++VC2+​]≃−2.05+3E​

The extra slope is physical: the separated products carry three more positive charges than the initial divacancy, with the electron reservoir included through their formation energies.

The attraction does not preferentially stabilize intact VV. It lowers the energy of the fragmentation products faster.

Three qualifications prevent this from becoming an unjustified destruction claim:

  • These are zero-temperature electronic formation energies. Vibrational free energies can move the crossing.
  • Separated-defect energies do not supply the short-range escape pathway.
  • The charged fragments repel one another. Two +2+2+2 fragments have a continuum Coulomb interaction of approximately 0.59 eV at 1 nm separation using the same dielectric constant. That contribution cannot be discarded when joining the bound intermediate to the separated endpoint.

Mixing entropy must also enter a full dissociation equilibrium. A positive standard formation-energy difference alone does not establish stability at a particular dilute defect concentration.

The conclusion is therefore specific: the collector needs kinetic protection against a chemically plausible, increasingly favourable fragmentation branch. Constraining a simulation to intact divacancies would remove precisely the process that can reverse the result.

3. Reversible collection works in the model, but remains modest in the finite construction

I retained the source-based complementary pivot rates, with the earlier explicit assumptions:

  • attempt frequency 1013 s−110^{13}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}1013 s−1;
  • unit charge-state statistical weights;
  • return factor 1/21/21/2 for the antisite-mediated pivot;
  • the supplied energy barriers, initially without activation-entropy corrections.

The charged pathway calculations supply the pivot geometry and barriers; they do not supply every possible escape from the antisite intermediate or a complete dissociation network. link.aps.org

The spatial transport equation is

∂tc=∂x ⁣[D(x)(∂xc+βF′(x)c)],\partial_t c = \partial_x\!\left[ D(x)\left(\partial_xc+\beta F'(x)c\right) \right],∂t​c=∂x​[D(x)(∂x​c+βF′(x)c)],

with both D(x)D(x)D(x) and F(x)F(x)F(x) obtained from the same local charge populations.

For defects initially 20 nm away, the calculated probability of occupying the central 10 nm is:

ConstructionAt 24 hoursAt 72 hoursLargest occupation found over stopping time
Uniform material, ordinary charge-equilibrated annealing11.5%11.0%12.1%, around 36 hours
Ideal, fully ionized sheet, 1012 cm−210^{12}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}1012 cm−20.58%8.9%25.7%, around 600 hours
Finite 20 nm Al profile, including ionization0.59%8.1%20.1%, around 470 hours

These are new model results without chemical loss, not measured yields. The finite-layer result changed by approximately 0.002 percentage points when the spatial mesh was halved. Adding the known intermediate populations consistently to equilibrium storage and transport changed the peak by less than 0.01 percentage points.

The low intermediate populations therefore justify a small correction to the transport calculation. They do not justify ignoring chemical risk.

The times are uncertain; the weak collection result is not merely a slow-clock artefact

The published neutral silicon-vacancy pivot has a calculated activation-free-energy reduction of 0.37 eV at 1,500 K. Charged-path entropy corrections were not acquired in that study. link.aps.org

As a source-based sensitivity test, I extrapolated that one correction linearly to 1,200 K, giving 0.296 eV, and left the other corrections unchanged. This is deliberately a partial correction:

  • the best stopping time fell from about 470 to 61 hours;
  • the peak target occupation changed from 20.1% to 21.1%.

Giving both fast pivot legs the same correction shortened the time further but left the peak near 20%. Thus, accelerating the clock is not sufficient to turn this collector into reliable placement.

Nor is 20% a global ceiling. Stronger layers collected more. An especially narrow, assumed 5 nm layer with ten times the Al inventory reached about 51% at 3,000 hours and was still improving. That case requires a sharper construction, has a larger population of the antisite intermediate, and places the centre in the fragmentation-favoured energetic regime. It cannot be granted those resources without their chemical consequences.

Cooling can retain a successful position without an irreversible chemical trap. Under the baseline two-charge rates, even maintaining the maximum 1,200 K diffusivity for an additional minute would add only about 0.73 nm of three-dimensional RMS displacement. This supplies a conditional cooling requirement; it does not establish an experimental cooling cycle or increase the fraction that arrived.

4. Why the attractive well supplies less directed motion than expected

The published network does not acquire this complete interface. The 2024 work explicitly limits its vacancy-separation configurations and does not calculate full dissociation into isolated monovacancies. link.aps.org

There is a second material interface at the collector itself: bulk defect energetics do not supply defect–Al binding and migration near an actual dopant. The smooth space-charge model specifies a field, but cannot silently grant the local chemistry of the atoms producing it.

The annealing, charge-assisted formation and feedback-placement results are experimentally realised benchmarks. Their numerical performance cannot simply be transferred between materials or equated with relocation of an existing complex. researchgate.net+2

The prospective distinction remains worthwhile: moving existing complexes without a new vacancy-generation step. But this construction currently supplies a conditional layer-collection operation. It does not yet supply reliable individual placement, preservation of useful silicon-vacancy spectators, or restoration of a neutral spin-active readout state inside the Al-rich destination.

I am retaining the collector calculation and its failures, while moving the scientific emphasis from the mobility optimum to selectivity of the complete translation-and-escape network. The requirements are now concrete:

  • the attractive destination must remain compatible with the transition states that carry translation;
  • the same destination must not make a competing chemical family overwhelmingly easier to reach;
  • escape must be suppressed over the accumulated residence in every reactive waypoint;
  • the atoms producing the destination must have compatible local chemistry.

The present evidence establishes those coupled constraints and gives quantitative escape-barrier targets. It does not yet establish a superior atomic-placement treatment. Further work earns its value by changing or acquiring that chemical interface; another adjustment of the Fermi-level setting cannot substitute for it.
